title: Sprint entropy KPI and contingency log
content:
Purpose:
Quick working log for measuring 'sprint entropy' (drift in readiness + increasing variance in KPIs) and a compact contingency + rollback playbook for launches. This is intentionally scrappy — notes, hypotheses, and actionable checks for the next two sprints.

Scope:
- Applies to staged launches (canary -> ramp) for product and infra changes that affect inference routing, capacity, or cost controls.
- Intended for product-ops, SRE, serving runtime, and release engineering.

Definitions (working):
- Sprint entropy: a single heuristic combining leading-indicator volatility (stddev over 24h windows) + number of unresolved release blockers. Higher is bad.
- Leading indicators: short-lived signals that tend to precede SLO regressions (latency tail, q95 increase, cache miss rate spikes, failed rollouts).

Leading indicators to track (daily):
- q95 p99 latency delta (canary vs baseline) — target: < +10%
- Error rate spike (5m window) — tolerance: < 0.2% absolute increase
- KV cache miss ratio — target: < 8%
- Token cost per 1k tokens (canary vs baseline) — flag if > +15%
- Model fallback frequency — flag if > 1 per 1k requests
- Deployment blocker count (unresolved JIRAs with severity >= P2) — aim: 0

KPI tracker snapshot (format: metric — target / current / urgency):
- q95 latency — <= 120ms / 132ms / medium
- p99 latency — <= 350ms / 420ms / high
- request error rate — <= 0.5% / 0.67% / medium-high
- cost per token — baseline 0.75c / 0.86c / low
- successful canary requests (%) — >= 99.5% / 98.9% / medium
- KV cache hit rate — >= 92% / 88% / medium-high

Entropy score (daily quick calc):
- Components: normalized latency volatility (0-1), normalized error spike (0-1), unresolved blocker fraction (0-1).
- Quick heuristic: Entropy = 0.5*latency_vol + 0.3*error_spike + 0.2*blocker_frac.
- Action thresholds: <0.25 green, 0.25-0.5 yellow (review), >0.5 red (hold/rollback).

Preflight checklist (pre-canary, owner initials):
- [ ] Canary target population defined (SE / data-driven) — owner: OP
- [ ] Baseline window and query set captured (30d recent; 3 canonical SLs) — owner: DS
- [ ] Smoke eval suite recorded + acceptance criteria (pass >= 97%) — owner: QA
- [ ] Rollback toggle verified in infra (feature flag + traffic cut) — owner: PLAT
- [ ] Cost guardrails configured (alert at +10% cost delta) — owner: FIN/ENG
- [ ] Observability dashboard pinned + alert runbook linked — owner: SRE
- [ ] Runbook owners paged and on-call aware of windows — owner: ENG-RELEASE

Canary run (0-24h):
- Sample size: small fraction (0.5-2%) or controlled seed set.
- Live checks (every 5m): latency q95, error rate, cache miss ratio, fallback count, cost delta.
- If any single critical metric trips (p99 > 2x baseline OR error rate spike > 1.5% absolute): immediate pause and triage.
- If entropy > 0.5 for two consecutive checks (10m): cut traffic to baseline.

Contingency + rollback playbook (short form):
1) Triage step 0 (automated):
   - Automatic traffic cut to 0% for canary if critical alert fires. Tag incident 'auto-cut'.
2) If auto-cut happened:
   - Notify channel #prodops-launch (ping owners).
   - Grab last 30m traces and top 5 stacktraces.
   - Collect sentinel metrics (latency distribution, error types, model fallback reasons).
3) Human triage (SRE + Serving + Product-ops):
   - If root cause is infra (GPU OOM, kernel crash, network egress): rollback + incident.
   - If root cause is model regression (nonsensical outputs or decoding loops): rollback + model-tag rollback; open model-qa ticket.
   - If root cause is configuration (batching change, quantization flag): revert config and re-run canary on subset.
4) Post-rollback checklist:
   - Create incident stub in JIRA, label "launch-rollback" and assign owners.
   - Short post-mortem note in this doc with links (next section).

Escalation matrix (fast):
- Tier 1: on-call SRE + canary owner (15 min)
- Tier 2: serving runtime tech lead + release engineer (30 min)
- Exec notice: product lead + eng manager (60 min) if user-facing SLA > 10k users affected

Example failure modes & rapid mitigations (cheat sheet):
- p99 spike due to batch sizing: reduce max_batch_size via flag -> monitor next 10m
- Cache miss storm after TTL tweak: restore TTL and warm cache from snapshot
- Model variant fallback loops: pin to stable model variant and cut canary traffic
- Cost runaway (quantization misconfig): revert quantization flag and alert finance

Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress):
- How to automate entropy calc into dashboard (prefer PromQL + a small lambda)? TODO @Omar
- Agree on final weights for entropy composite (current heuristic is arbitrary) — propose an A/B of weights next retro
- Add a small synthetic traffic generator for stable smoke tests during canary — TODO @Diego

Post-incident micro-template (fill after any rollback):
- Date/time: 
- Canary id / tag: 
- Entropy score pre-cut: 
- Primary metric failed: 
- Root cause (short): 
- Immediate fix applied: 
- Follow-ups (owners + due dates): 

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc short and actionable. If it grows big, split into: (1) playbook (final) and (2) logbook (chronological).
- We want a single graph that shows entropy vs. p99 on one axis for quick visual correlation.

Recent log entries:
- 2024-11-20 — dry-run canary, entropy 0.18 (green). Found flaky metric label mapping in dashboard; fixed.
- 2024-11-28 — small ramp to 5% aborted manually after p99 jump; manual rollback applied; incident JIRA: PRODOPS-1129.

References / links:
- Confluence draft: PRODOPS-827-entropy-playbook
- Canary runbook (internal): github:repo/launch-scripts#42
- Incident: JIRA:PRODOPS-1129

Last quick note: this is a working artifact. Add your short logs below, date-stamped, and keep the playbook lean.
